page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical AMD EPYC 9T24 cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz and includes a 32 MB L3 cache. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance falls into the average category, as seen in the stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core tests. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with both small-block cached and large-block uncached read-only bandwidth testing in the bottom 25%, though large-block write bandwidth remains average. Computational workloads utilizing vector extensions benefit from hardware support for AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI.

Due to the weak performance in database operations, redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput, this instance is less suited for high-throughput storage or database-heavy applications. The lack of local storage requires external block storage attachment. The instance is best suited for compute-bound workloads that rely on strong single-thread performance, such as text processing, lightweight cryptography tasks, and basic single-threaded compression or decompression pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized virtual server featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor running at 2.7 GHz. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of RAM, 32 MB of L3 cache, and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps, with no local storage or GPU. Benchmarks show strong single-core CPU and text processing performance, though multi-core scaling and memory read bandwidth are weaker. The instance supports advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and AES cryptography. It is best suited for compute-bound, single-threaded tasks, text processing, and lightweight utility workloads rather than memory-intensive databases or high-throughput web serving.
